**Support Manager**

Cenorion · Dubai, DIFC · Early-stage, pre-launch

A billion people are creditworthy and invisible to the system. We are building the infrastructure that sees them.

Cenorion is an early-stage company building a device-financing and device-management platform for emerging markets. We are preparing for our first commercial launch, and this is the first appointment in that sequence.

You will build and run the service function from nothing. Not a queue to maintain: the support model, the tooling, the policies and the runbooks, and the operational requirements that have to be built into the platform before we go live.

**What you will do**

* Own the support model end to end: severity levels, response targets, coverage and escalation from first line into second and third.
* Decide what the operation needs and get it built into the platform before launch, including the operating record that lets any event be reconstructed.
* Select, implement and configure our service desk platform, with Zendesk as the intended choice.
* Write the support policy, process and runbook set from nothing, and get people to follow it.
* Run second line yourself for the first deployment, then build and lead the team as volume grows.
* Own incident response and the reviews that make the platform stronger each time.

**What we are looking for**

* Around seven years or more in technical support or service delivery for B2B software or platforms, with three or more leading second line or a service delivery function.
* You have implemented a service desk platform, not only worked inside one. Zendesk specifically is a strong advantage.
* You have written support policy and process from nothing, and managed people through it.
* Real incident management experience, where the answer you gave mattered.
* Bonus: fintech, payments or other regulated services; Android or mobile device management; ITIL or equivalent; partners across several countries.

Building a service function from nothing and running real incidents are the hard gates. Everything else we flex on.

Dubai-based, on-site, close to leadership and engineering. UAE-based candidates only for this round. If you want to build a service function rather than inherit one, let us talk.

**Job Description**
Business Operations Manager
  
  

* Business Development
* Dubai, UAE
* Justlife

Right now, thousands of people in the UAE book a cleaner through Justlife and expect them to show up on time, do excellent work, and leave their home better than they found it. That promise only holds if the cleaners are there, trained, motivated, and routed efficiently — which means someone has to own the daily operating reality of that supply chain: keeping cleaners deployed, partners accountable, costs disciplined, and quality high.
  
  
This is an operations role, not a strategy role. Youll run the DTC home cleaning business end-to-end — 300+ cleaners across multiple partner companies, a small on-ground team of account executives and roster agents, and measurable improvement in on-time performance, completion rates, and contribution margin within your first six months. Every day youll make decisions that move the numbers: which partner hires next, how to incentivise productivity, where fuel and routing waste money, whether were hitting our supply plan. This is what it means to own a real business line.
  
  
Youll love this role if you...
  
  

* You think in unit economics and get frustrated when a cost lever stays hidden in a spreadsheet instead of being fixed
* Youve run a large field or blue-collar workforce (directly or through partners) and know exactly how to hold external teams accountable without being their boss
* Youre energised by problems you can see and touch — youd rather spend an hour in a van or at a partner accommodation than sit in a meeting
* You build teams that work without you, and you actively coach people into bigger roles
* You obsess over data quality because you know bad reports kill decisions, and youll learn SQL or Power BI yourself rather than wait for someone to build your dashboard

What youll own
  
  

* Drive sustained improvement in on-time %, completion rate %, promise-kept %, and absent rate % by building daily operating discipline — reviewing metrics with the team each morning, identifying blockers, and acting on them before they compound into service failures.
* Lead and develop the on-ground operations team (2 account executives and 4 remote roster agents): set clear priorities, review performance daily, coach individuals toward higher capability, and manage accountability.
* Own supply planning and growth: forecast cleaner headcount needed against demand by city and partner, manage onboarding pace and allocation across partner companies, and reduce time-to-deployment so new hires contribute faster.
* Manage partner companies as senior counterparts: run monthly business reviews, hold them to service-level agreements and commercial terms, reconcile statements of account with finance monthly, and escalate issues before they become crises.
* Design and drive cost and process projects that improve contribution margin — incentive structure redesigns, fuel and fleet controls, van routing optimisation, cleaner orientation and training — taking each from idea to measurable result.
* Build and maintain reporting that surfaces whats driving performance: which partners are slipping, where attrition is highest, which cost levers moved margin, whats blocking supply. Act on what it shows.
* Spend meaningful time in the field — in vans, accommodations, and partner sites — so you understand problems first-hand and your team sees you do the same.

What tells us youre the one
  
  

* Youve measurably improved operational metrics across a large field workforce — tell us a specific program you ran (incentive redesign, routing optimisation, vendor onboarding, training rollout, etc.) and the metric that moved as a result: completion rate up X%, on-time performance improved Y%, attrition fell Z%, or margin lifted by N%.
* You can spot cause and effect: when a metric moves, you know whether its partner execution, process design, incentive misalignment, or something else — and you know how to test your hypothesis before rolling out a fix.
* Youve managed blue-collar, field-based, or logistics workforces (home services, facilities management, staffing, last-mile delivery, quick commerce) — or run marketplace operations where supply quality depends on external partners. Results matter far more than years, but 5–7 years of this kind of work is the sweet spot.
* Youre fluent in data: you can build operating reports independently, interrogate a spreadsheet without help, and use SQL, Power BI, or AI tools to automate manual reporting so you have time to think.
* You speak fluent English, written and spoken. Bonus: you speak languages common to the workforce in the UAE (Tagalog, Urdu, Arabic), or you have prior experience operating in the UAE market in home services, logistics, or staffing.

Why Justlife
  
  

* Scale and impact: Youll run a real, revenue-generating business line serving thousands of customers across the UAE, managing hundreds of cleaners and multiple partner companies, with direct line of sight from your decisions to customer satisfaction and margin.
* Clear growth path: this role is a launchpad into broader category leadership, multi-city operations, or general management as we scale across the GCC.
* Close partnership with leadership: youll work alongside the Business Development lead and the founding team, with real influence on strategy and resource decisions.
* A fair, performance-driven culture: youll be measured on the metrics you own, recognised through our JustHeroes program, and rewarded for results — not politics.
* Startup benefits: a birthday day off (JustHoliday), free Justlife service credits, referral bonuses, and regular team experiences.

**About us**

The Institute of Making is a unique organisation that explores, celebrates, and investigates materials and processes through a wide range of activities. From large-scale public events to ground-breaking academic research projects, our diverse outputs and many audiences are united by a shared passion for materials and making. On a day-to-day basis, we bring together students and staff from across UCL, to provide a creative home in which to collaborate, innovate, contemplate and experience making from a wide range of disciplines. At the heart of the Institute of Making are our open-access facilities, which include multi-material workshops and the Materials Library.

The Institute of Making opened in Bloomsbury in 2013 with a workshop offering a broad range of tools and machinery for inducted members to use. The Materials Library is an ever-expanding repository of some of the most extraordinary materials on earth, including shape memory alloys and self-healing materials as well as some of the more ordinary materials that have also changed the world, like paper, beeswax, and copper. The Workshop and our Materials Library sit side-by-side, enabling users to experience first-hand the relationships between materials and tools that constitute processes of making. The space is also a stage for our expansive events programme and a home to a multitude of research projects.

The Institute of Making workshop team is responsible for establishing the safe and sustainable operation of the workshops and supporting our members in using the equipment and facilities across both the Bloomsbury and Stratford sites. The team’s main duties include supervising members’ access to the space, inducting new members, conducting tool trainings, advising members on design, materials, and processes, supporting the delivery of events, and contributing to the friendly, welcoming, imaginative, and open-minded atmosphere of the Institute of Making.

**Job Summary:**

The Sr. Manager, MENA Supply Chain is the single-threaded owner of end-to-end logistics performance and build-out across the Middle East and North Africa region, with initial focus on the GCC (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman). This role designs, launches, and scales the regional logistics network, ensuring best-in-class cost, service, and delivery speed.

Operating as a core member of the regional leadership team, this role is the primary partner to the COO in-region. It translates global logistics strategy into scalable, high-performing operations and shapes key decisions based on regional realities, including cross-border customs flows, Arabic labeling, cash on delivery, and seasonal demand peaks such as Ramadan, Eid, and White Friday.

This is a hands-on leadership role combining strategy, execution, and team building during a critical scale-up phase.

**Job Expectations:**

### **Build and Own the MENA Supply Chain Setup**

  

* Lead the end-to-end setup of the MENA logistics network, including selection of the regional hub (for example a free zone warehouse in Dubai) and the set-up of an Arabic and bilingual labeling solution in the MENA warehouse.
* Define the flow model for the region: import and consolidation at the hub, in-country distribution, and cross-border linehaul to the other GCC markets and, over time, the wider MENA region.
* Ensure the initial setup is scalable, cost-efficient, and operationally robust.
* Ensure logistics is a proactive enabler of growth, not a constraint.

### **End-to-End Performance Ownership**

  

* Own regional logistics KPIs across (i) cost (transport, warehousing, handling, customs duties and fees), (ii) service levels (OTIF, delivery promise accuracy, first-attempt delivery, cash on delivery remittance accuracy), and (iii) speed (lead times, delivery SLAs by country and city tier).
* Drive trade-off decisions across transportation, warehousing, and inventory, including air versus sea inbound and hub versus in-country stock placement.
* Plan capacity and inventory for regional demand peaks (Ramadan, Eid, White Friday) and for summer heat constraints on temperature-sensitive products.
* Establish full visibility and control over performance drivers.

### **Strategic Partner to COO (Regional Translation and Feedback Loop)**

  

* Act as the go-to logistics counterpart to the COO in MENA.
* Translate global strategy into executable regional plans.
* Provide structured feedback to global teams on (i) market constraints, (ii) performance gaps, and (iii) optimization opportunities.
* Proactively challenge and refine global assumptions based on MENA realities, such as address quality, last-mile variability, and payment preferences.

### **Customs, Compliance and Regulatory Coordination**

  

* Drive cross-functional coordination to ensure MENA regulatory requirements are met across logistics operations, including product registration and import approvals with the relevant authorities in each market (for example SFDA in Saudi Arabia and the competent health and standards authorities in the UAE), GCC and country-level customs procedures, and halal and conformity requirements where applicable.
* Partner with Compliance, Legal, Marketing, customs brokers, and external partners on Arabic labeling, documentation (certificates of origin, attestations, import permits), and market-specific requirements.
* Translate compliance needs into operational execution across warehouses, 3PLs, customs brokers, and distribution flows, including free zone and mainland transfers and the GCC customs transit process.
* Identify risks and dependencies, such as shipment holds, registration delays, and duty classification disputes, and drive resolution across stakeholders.

### **Team Build and Leadership**

  

* Act as logistics representative within the regional leadership team.
* Lead a lean, high-performing regional logistics team, including a 3PL /Warehouse Manager, a Transportation and Customs Manager, and an Inventory Planner, with the ability to build a multi-cultural team across the region.
* Coach the team on carrier, 3PL, and customs broker strategy and execution, and collaborate with global to ensure global strategy and guardrails are followed.

### **Continuous Optimization and Scale**

  

* Identify and execute cost and efficiency improvements early.
* Optimize network design (warehouse footprint, in-country versus hub stock, routing, inventory placement), including the timing of a second node, for example in Saudi Arabia, as volumes grow.
* Optimize last-mile and cash on delivery operations, including carrier mix, delivery success rates, and returns handling.
* Lead regional logistics projects (process improvements, system enhancements).

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:**

Required:

* Proven experience building or scaling logistics operations (warehouse, transport, and inventory) in the region.
* Strong hands-on experience with 3PLs, carrier networks, customs brokers, and multi-country GCC distribution, including cross-border trucking and free zone operations.
* Working knowledge of GCC customs procedures and import requirements for regulated consumer products (health, food, personal care).
* Experience with e-commerce last-mile, including cash on delivery and returns, is strongly preferred.
* Proven ability to influence and align cross-functional stakeholders without direct authority.
* Experience operating in ambiguous, fast-scaling environments.
* Ability to operate at both strategic and deeply operational levels.
* Strong stakeholder management across global and regional teams, and the cultural fluency to work with partners across different MENA markets.
* Data-driven, execution-focused, and comfortable making trade-offs.
* Fluent English is required. Arabic is a strong advantage.

**Equipment Knowledge:**

  

* Experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
* Experience with Google Business Suite (Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Forms) preferred

**Experience Requirements:**

Generally requires a minimum 10 years in logistics / supply chain, with strong MENA or GCC exposure.

**Travel Requirements:**

The role is based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, with frequent travel to the hub warehouse and port areas (for example Jebel Ali) and regular travel to other markets in the region, in particular Saudi Arabia (Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam).

**Education Requirements:**

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, a related discipline or equivalent additional experience required

Gulbahar Tobacco International (GTI) is seeking a proactive, commercially driven Travel Retail Executive to support the continued expansion and management of its Global Travel Retail business.

With a rapidly growing presence across international airports and partnerships with leading duty-free operators, the successful candidate will play a central role in managing day-to-day commercial activities, coordinating with retail partners, and ensuring the effective execution of GTI's commercial and marketing initiatives across the channel.

The position requires strong account management, analytical, and coordination capabilities, with the ability to independently manage multiple accounts and projects across different markets.

The Travel Retail Executive will serve as the primary operational point of contact between GTI, its duty-free partners, and internal departments, ensuring commercial plans are translated into measurable results.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Travel Retail Account Management:**

* Manage day-to-day commercial relationships and operational communication with existing duty-free operators.
* Act as the main coordination point for account-related inquiries, operational requirements, and commercial follow-ups.
* Maintain regular communication with duty-free operators to review sales performance, stock availability, product assortment, and ongoing commercial activities.
* Monitor the implementation of agreed commercial terms, including pricing, margins, listing fees, promotional commitments, and payment conditions.
* Maintain an updated database of accounts, airports, retail locations, contacts, commercial agreements, and key account requirements.
* Support management in preparing business reviews and identifying opportunities to improve account performance.

**Sales Performance, Reporting & Analysis:**

* Collect, consolidate, and analyse periodic sales reports from duty-free operators, with visibility by airport, terminal, shop, brand, and SKU wherever available.
* Develop and maintain monthly sales dashboards tracking actual performance against forecasts and targets.
* Identify sales trends, underperforming SKUs, and opportunities to improve product assortment and retail performance.
* Monitor retail selling prices, competitive positioning, and relevant market developments across airports.
* Coordinate with retail partners to establish consistent sales reporting schedules and ensure timely receipt of accurate data.
* Prepare monthly account performance reviews with key findings, recommendations, and follow-up actions.

**Planning, Inventory & Order Management:**

* Coordinate with duty-free operators to obtain regular stock reports and monitor inventory levels by SKU and retail location.
* Work closely with GTI's Demand Planning, Production, and Logistics teams to develop rolling sales forecasts and replenishment requirements.
* Proactively identify potential out-of-stock situations and recommend timely replenishment orders.
* Coordinate purchase orders from confirmation through production, shipment, delivery, and receipt.
* Monitor stock coverage, inventory ageing, and slow-moving products, recommending corrective actions where necessary.
* Maintain visibility over lead times, shipment schedules, and operational constraints affecting product availability.

**New Listings & Business Expansion:**

* Follow up with partners on launch schedules, initial purchase orders, stock delivery, and retail readiness.
* Support the preparation of commercial presentations, account proposals, and business development materials.

**Marketing & Retail Execution:**

* Coordinate with GTI's Marketing team and duty-free operators to implement agreed trade marketing activities, promotional campaigns, and brand visibility initiatives.
* Monitor the installation and maintenance of branded displays, gondolas, point-of-sale materials (POSM), and other merchandising assets.
* Ensure the agreed product assortment, shelf placement, and brand visibility standards are maintained across retail locations.
* Coordinate promotional calendars, in-store activations, and seasonal commercial initiatives with retail partners.
* Monitor the execution of marketing commitments, including display rentals, promotional placements, and other agreed investments.
* Gather photographic evidence, retail feedback, and execution reports to assess the effectiveness of marketing activities.

**Brand Ambassador & Agency Coordination:**

* Coordinate with appointed Brand Ambassador and merchandising agencies supporting GTI's Travel Retail operations.
* Monitor staffing deployment, attendance, retail coverage, and compliance with agreed service requirements.
* Collect and review Brand Ambassador sales and activity reports.
* Coordinate product training, promotional briefs, and brand-related communication in collaboration with Marketing.
* Track agency performance against agreed KPIs and escalate execution gaps where necessary.
* Support the evaluation of promotional activities and Brand Ambassador effectiveness in driving incremental sales.

**Commercial Administration & Financial Coordination:**

* Maintain accurate records of commercial agreements, pricing structures, listing fees, promotional budgets, and account-specific financial commitments.
* Coordinate with Finance on sales reconciliations, invoicing, payment follow-ups, and outstanding receivables.
* Support monthly reconciliation of consignment sales and inventory for accounts operating under consignment arrangements.
* Validate reported sales quantities, applicable commercial deductions, marketing fees, and settlement amounts against agreed commercial terms.
* Track approved trade marketing expenditure and ensure supporting documentation is maintained.
* Highlight commercial discrepancies, unapproved changes, or potential financial exposure to management.

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):**

Performance will be assessed against a combination of commercial, operational, and execution-related indicators:

* **Sales Performance:** Achievement of sales targets and growth across assigned Travel Retail accounts.
* **Product Availability:** Stock availability, stock coverage, and reduction of avoidable out-of-stock incidents.
* **Forecast Accuracy:** Reliability of sales forecasts and replenishment recommendations.
* **Reporting Discipline:** Timely submission and accuracy of sales, stock, and account performance reports.

* **Agency Performance:** Brand Ambassador coverage, reporting compliance, and achievement of agreed performance objectives.
* **Financial Follow-Up:** Timely sales reconciliation, invoicing coordination, and resolution of outstanding payment issues.

You will own internal IT end to end — identity and access, SaaS services, workstations and the corporate network that every colleague relies on daily. You'll lead a team of five administrators and take charge of the subscription budget, quarterly planning and renewals. We give you real decision-making authority: only spend above the limit, headcount or key vendor changes, risk acceptance and company-wide changes go up for approval. Everything else is your call, within the boundaries set out under "Decision Rights".

**You'll take ownership of:**

This is a hands-on lead role. Roughly 30% of your time goes to people, planning and alignment, and 70% to hands-on work: complex changes, incident investigation, configuration reviews, automation. You set up routine work so that it runs without you.

**1. Team and quarterly planning**

* Lead five administrators: 1:1s, goals, feedback. Run hiring for approved positions and, when necessary, parting ways — the latter agreed with your manager.
* Organize work across time zones: open incidents are handed over in writing to a specific person, and inconvenient hours are shared fairly. Three time zones cover about 13 hours of the working day, but not 24/7: you decide what truly requires a night-time or weekend response.
* Every critical system has a primary administrator and a backup who knows how to restore it.
* Each quarter, bring a plan: goals, owners, a support buffer and a list of what did not make the cut. Base it on feedback from engineers, recurring incidents and the renewal calendar. At the end of the quarter, show what was done, what was not and why. If urgent work comes up mid-quarter, say what moves and at what cost.
* Prepare a monthly report for the area: service and support health, access status, subscription spend and optimization results, key risks and items that need a management decision.

**2. Identity and access reviews**

* The identity provider is the central point of access provisioning: SSO, phishing-resistant MFA, role-based groups, SCIM. Hiring, transfers and terminations are triggered from the HR system.
* You verify revocation in the application itself. Deactivating a user in the identity provider does not end active sessions or revoke API tokens, local accounts and guest access. Systems without SCIM have an owner for manual revocation, and you make sure it is done.
* Access review frequency depends on risk: privileged and financial systems quarterly, everything else every six months. The system owner decides on each access, revocation is confirmed in the target system, and every exception has a reason and an expiry date. Results are retained as audit evidence.

**3. Corporate services and developer support**

* **Zero Trust access and DNS:** Zero Trust for internal tools (access policies, secure web gateway, device posture) and DNS for corporate domains. Policy changes roll out to a limited group first, and the on-call engineer has a rollback procedure. WAF and the product perimeter stay with DevOps.
* **Cloud, corporate side:** Cloud SSO integrated with the identity provider, role assignments agreed with DevOps, sandbox accounts, spend in corporate accounts. Organization structure and production belong to DevOps.
* **Corporate messaging:** Apps and integrations, guests and external channels, retention policies. Before a bot is installed, you know what data it reads and who owns it.
* **Collaboration suite:** Mail, calendar and documents: sharing rules, third-party OAuth apps, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, data transfer at offboarding.
* **Ticketing and knowledge base:** Permissions, projects and spaces, SSO sign-in. The ticketing system is the team's work queue, the knowledge base holds documentation.
* **Workstations:** MDM: encryption, updates, security policies, shipping a laptop to another country with zero-touch setup.
* Build self-service for developers: standard access is requested via chat or a ticket, approved by the resource owner and granted automatically for a limited time.
* Set support priorities: major outages and security incidents first, then requests that block teams from working.
* Together with DevOps, define clear ownership boundaries and drive shared requests to resolution: a ticket is closed when the problem is solved for the user, not when it has been handed to another team.

**4. Subscriptions and costs**

* Maintain the SaaS registry: owner, cost, number of seats, actual usage, renewal date and the last day the order can still be changed.
* Review paid seats separately from access reviews. Once a month, reconcile paid seats against activity. Long inactivity is a reason to check with the owner, not to reclaim the seat automatically: there are break-glass accounts and tools that are only needed once a quarter.
* Plan each contract review backwards from the last day the order can be changed or the renewal cancelled. By that day, the volume is agreed, the negotiation position is ready and the vendor has been notified if required. Example: 80 editor seats are paid for, 30 are actively used — we go to the vendor with 35 and a question about the pricing tier.
* Find shadow IT through OAuth grants and corporate card spend. In corporate cloud accounts, analyze bill growth by account and service together with the resource owner. Measure savings against invoices, separating realized savings from those expected at the next renewal.

**5. AI and automation**

For you, AI is the normal way the whole team works. What we expect:

* First-line support in chat: answers from the knowledge base with source links, request classification and ticket creation, handing unclear cases to a human.
* Preparation of access reviews and license reviews: AI reconciles exports from the identity provider, the HR system and applications and produces a list of anomalies for an administrator to verify.

* Set the rules: what data may be shared with a model and where only a human makes the decision. AI does not grant privileged access or reset MFA: an administrator does that, verifying the employee's identity before any MFA reset.

* Drive productivity, cost efficiency and continuous improvement initiatives.

* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure smooth operations.
* Promote safety, accountability and a high-performance culture.

**Requirements:**

**Key Responsibilities**
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

* Constraint Management
* Proactively identify current and future material and supplier capacity constraints.
* Own constraint management and shortage resolution at plant level.
* Coordinate with Production Planning to maintain an aligned constraint and delivery horizon.
* Analyse demand, open orders, supplier commitments and inventory coverage to identify potential shortages before production is impacted.
* Establish recovery plans for constrained materials with clear actions, owners and completion dates.
* Support inventory optimisation by highlighting excess, shortage and coverage risks to the Planning team.
* Maintain visibility and reporting of critical constraints through to closure.
* Escalate unresolved capacity, quality or delivery risks through the appropriate Procurement channels.
* Supplier Delivery Performance & Expediting
* Manage supplier delivery performance at plant level, including OTD/OTIF, overdue orders and repeated delivery failures.
* Expedite critical materials as the first-line resolver.
* Obtain firm and realistic recovery commitments from suppliers for delayed materials.
* Prioritise expediting activities according to production requirements and line-down risk.
* Conduct root-cause analysis of delivery failures using 5-Why, 8D or equivalent methodologies.
* Agree and track supplier corrective actions through to sustainable closure.
* Identify recurring supplier delivery issues and escalate them to the relevant RCM/GCM for further supplier or commercial intervention.
* Work with Logistics, Planning and suppliers to minimise emergency freight while protecting production continuity.
* Supplier Capacity & Production Constraints
* Assess supplier capacity against current demand, forecasts and future production requirements.
* Identify potential capacity bottlenecks before they become delivery constraints.
* Understand supplier manufacturing processes, equipment, tooling, cycle times, shift patterns, manpower and raw-material constraints.

* Coordinate supplier recovery and capacity improvement plans where capacity is insufficient.
* Monitor agreed capacity actions and investments through to implementation.
* Escalate structural capacity constraints requiring sourcing, investment or commercial support to Procurement/RCM/GCM.
* Support alternate-source development where capacity or continuity risk cannot be adequately mitigated.
* Disruption & Escalation Management
* Mitigate line-down risk and coordinate emergency supply actions before impact on production.
* Lead plant-level response to critical supplier shortages and delivery disruptions.
* Coordinate Planning, Procurement, Logistics, Quality, Engineering and suppliers to establish immediate recovery actions.
* Exhaust first-line operational recovery options before escalating commercial leverage requirements to the RCM.
* Provide clear escalation covering:

+ Production impact
+ Material availability
+ Supplier commitment
+ Capacity position
+ Recovery actions
+ Required management support

* Ensure critical issues remain actively managed until material availability and supply stability are restored.

**Role Scope**

**Regulatory and Permits**

* Prepare and submit import permits and follow up with the relevant authorities until approved.

* Process online chemical permits through the relevant federal and local government authorities.
* Register cosmetic products and obtain the required approvals before import.

* Make sure dangerous goods are classified, packed, labelled and documented under IATA DGR / IMDG, with valid Safety Data Sheets.

**Customs and Clearance**

* Prepare and submit import, export and re-export customs declarations on the relevant customs platforms, with the PRO team and licensed clearing agents.
* Make sure HS codes (UAE/GCC 12-digit), Incoterms 2020, origin, duty and import VAT are correct under the GCC Common Customs Law.
* Identify restricted or controlled items before goods are shipped.

* Process duty exemptions, temporary admissions, re-exports for overseas repair, and recovery of customs deposits.
* Collect, verify and maintain commercial invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, airway bills, certificates of origin and delivery orders.
* Track free time at the relevant ports and entry points to avoid demurrage, detention and storage charges.

**Logistics Coordination**

* Agree shipment mode and timelines with the Sourcing Team and recommend the most cost-effective option (sea, air, land, consolidation).
* Check forwarder quotations against approved rate cards and make sure shipping POs are raised in the ERP before goods move.
* Coordinate inbound and outbound shipments with 3PLs, freight forwarders and transporters, and maintain the shipment tracking register.
* Follow up on delays, and share ETAs and delivery orders with end users in advance so goods are handed over smoothly.
* Resolve damages, shortages and incorrect shipments, including cargo insurance claims and return-to-vendor shipments.
* Allocate freight, duty and clearance charges to the related POs, and follow up with Finance on invoices and advance payments.
* Track 3PL, forwarder and clearing agent performance against SLAs and provide input to quarterly reviews.

**Asset Disposal and Closure**

* Receive approved disposal forms and coordinate scrap, resale, write-off and environmentally compliant disposal in line with policy and the DoA.
* Track each disposal memo through Finance preparation, Miral Group approval and the audit schedule.
* Identify licensed buyers and recyclers with Procurement, and arrange site inspections.
* Obtain and compare at least two quotations (or as the DoA requires), and complete collection within the quotation's validity.
* Confirm payment from the buyer and the Finance receipt before releasing any item that generates income.
* Issue property removal forms and gate passes with Security, and obtain proof of dispatch, weighbridge tickets and the buyer's acknowledgement.
* Use only licensed contractors for hazardous waste and e-waste, and obtain transfer notes, recycling, destruction and data-wiping certificates.
* Hand a complete close-out pack to Finance so the asset register and gain or loss are updated in the ERP.

**Third-Party Access**

* Arrange site and port access permits for vendors, contractors and transporters.
* Keep authority registrations and access credentials valid and renewed on time.
* Verify contractor HSSE documents before work starts: IDs, PPE, forklift certificates and registration, inspection certificate, risk assessment and method statement.
* Raise a Permit to Work for disposal collections and other third-party logistics activities on site, and close it as soon as the work is complete.
* Coordinate collection and delivery schedules with site teams and Security.
* Make sure 3PL, transporter and contractor activities comply with Miral Group HSE and Security requirements.

**Compliance and Reporting**

* Track permit expiry dates, renewals and regulatory updates, and alert stakeholders in time.
* Keep logistics, permit and disposal records audit-ready, and support internal audit, ICFR and DoA reviews

* Maintain a live disposal tracker (status, items, value, buyer, open permits).
* Prepare monthly reports on freight cost, lead times, clearance, demurrage, permits and disposals.
* Track logistics spend against budget and flag variances to the Logistics / Supply Chain Manager.
* Keep SOPs, document templates and authority contact lists up to date.
* Support the set-up of logistics and disposal processes, and propose improvements such as consolidation and greener logistics.

**Key Performance Indicators**

Permit turnaround

Days from submission to approval; no expired permits or registrations.

Clearance time

Days from arrival to release; first-time-right declarations

On-time delivery

Share of shipments delivered by the agreed date

Disposal cycle time

Days from approved memo to collection; share of disposals fully closed out on time.

Zero compliance penalties

No fines, no avoidable demurrage or detention, no expired open Permits to Work.

Cost savings

Freight cost against budget, cost per shipment, and value recovered from disposals against quotations.

Here at Amazon we are looking to hire experienced Reliability Engineering Maintenance Planners to join the team.
  
  
PURPOSE OF THE JOB:
  
The Reliability Engineering Maintenance Planner based in Abu Dhabi is responsible for asset and spares management, preventative maintenance planning and machine history data. They are the site lead for the CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) software and are required to extract information from it to support the decision making of the site engineering manager.
  
  
RESPONSIBILITIES:
  

* Be the site level Subject Matter Expert (SME) on the CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System) software, train the local engineering team in its use and escalate issues as required to the EU team.
* Ensure the system is run in line with Amazon standards and participate in EU led projects and improvement programmes to roll out new functionality, procedures, scheduling or reports.
* Ensure site level equipment, spare parts and minimum holding levels are correctly recorded in the system in order to ensure technicians are never without the parts they need.
* Ensure the system accurately forecasts and assigned all required preventative maintenance to technicians within the team to provide a high level of equipment availability to our internal customers.
* Compile equipment information, performance metrics and machine histories and make recommendations for improvements based on their findings.
* Manage spare parts stock levels, place and track orders as required. Work with procurement and the wider EU network to find savings or efficiencies.

  
  
Key job responsibilities  
As RME Planner, you own the planning, spares and data side of site maintenance in APM, the Asset Performance Management system. You will:  
  
Analyze daily shift reports and booked labor against expected hours. You will reopen work orders with poor data quality and coach the owners.  
Schedule and assign work orders to shifts, keep OTTO scheduled 14 days out, and own the monthly Usage-Based Maintenance (UBM) input and review cycle.  
Manage spare parts: weekly cycle counts, stock health, requisitions on Min/Max, stockout follow-up, repairs and PO quality.  
Run warranty claims end to end, with claims submitted within 5 business days.  
Review costs against forecast and keep users, employees, shift patterns and the skills matrix current in APM.  
Support launches and retrofits: trackers, asset uploads, IOQ work orders, PM forecasting and RSPL receipt.  
Prepare the yearly PM plan review and the Planning & Scheduling sections of the Amazon Maintenance System (AMS) audit.  
  
A day in the life  
Start of shift: Review the previous shift's reports and the last 24 hours of booked labor. Flag any red deviations to the RME Manager and reopen work orders with weak data. Manage the RME DDD (RME Daily Dive Deep meeting)  
Daily Area Start-up Meeting (15 min): Support the RME Area Manager with the day's plan: overdue work, PMs, vendors on site and resourcing.  
Midday: Work in APM and OTTO to schedule work orders and run requisitions. Chase stockouts and vendors, and check warranty claims and PO backlog.  
Three times a week: Run a 15-minute PM and System Check quality inspection on work orders closed in the last 24 hours.  
Rest of the day: Weekly and monthly cycle work, such as cycle counts and discrepancy follow-up, dashboard and metrics review, the leadership meeting, the Ops sync and the long-term plan meeting. Launch and retrofit tasks fit in around these.  
End of day: Close the loop with feedback to technicians and supervisors, and update trackers and APM.

To drive the growth of workshop manufacturing and spare-parts sales across the GCC while strengthening customer relationships through regular visits and close engagement. The role focuses on analysing customer needs and installed equipment, identifying local manufacturing and replacement opportunities, promoting workshop capabilities, and converting opportunities into sustainable sales order intake.
  
  
The role also supports customer enquiries and coordinates non-conformance (NC) follow-up and resolution, working with Spare Parts, Workshop, Engineering, Procurement, Quality, Logistics, Finance and back offices, as well as customers, vendors, suppliers and subcontractors.
  
  
**Key Accountabilities & Responsibilities**
**Close Customer Relationship & Visits**

* Make regular customer and site visits, particularly to key aluminium and industrial customers in the UAE and across the GCC.
* Understand customers’ installed equipment, operational issues and upcoming spare-part requirements.
* Develop strong relationships with end users and procurement teams.
* Encourage customers to include FSG in more requests for quotations (RFQs).

**Grow Workshop Sales & Develop Workshop Opportunities**

* Identify spare-parts and local fabrication opportunities.
* Promote the new workshop capabilities to customers.
* Build a pipeline of opportunities and follow them through to the RFQ and purchase-order (PO) stages.
* Understand customers’ replacement needs and proactively recommend spare parts before they are required.
* Coordinate with the workshop team on feasibility, lead times and costing.
* Manage consignment stock initiation and tracking.

**Installed-Base and Market Development**

* Build a good understanding of equipment installed at each customer site for both product lines.
* Identify obsolete, critical and frequently consumed spare parts.
* Maintain a list of opportunities, RFQs, quotations and expected orders.
* Predict spare-parts opportunities based on equipment lifetime.

**Customer Enquiries & Business Support**

* Receive, register and follow up customer RFQs, ensuring part references, quantities, drawings, specifications and required delivery dates are clearly identified.
* Maintain regular contact with assigned customers and coordinate regular visits.
* Identify potential parts for local fabrication at the workshop and refer opportunities to the workshop and engineering teams for feasibility assessment.
* Promote workshop capabilities in coordination with other departments and follow up open offers to support order conversion and repeat business.

**Reporting & Continuous Improvement**

* Prepare and analyse sales reports, tracking workshop sales order intake (SOI), spare-parts sales, conversion rates, margins and sales growth.
* Forecast future sales and identify opportunities for coming years based on installed equipment, part lifetime, replacement cycles and customer requirements.
* Monitor quoted versus actual costs and highlight variations affecting margins.
* Track open RFQs, outstanding orders and delivery status.
* Support continuous improvement of the enquiry-to-delivery process and maintain historical data to support future sales opportunities.

**Minimum Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering or a related technical discipline.
* Minimum of five (5) years of experience in spare-parts coordination, technical sales support or order processing within an industrial, manufacturing or workshop environment.
* Experience coordinating quotations, customer orders and deliveries with workshop and procurement teams.
* Aluminium smelter experience is mandatory.
* Exposure to machining and fabrication is an advantage.

**PROFESSIONAL KNOWLEDGE, CERTIFICATION OR MEMBERSHIPs**

* Understanding of spare-parts identification, mechanical drawings, material specifications and basic manufacturing processes, including machining and fabrication.
* Knowledge of RFQ handling, costing inputs, quotation preparation, purchase-order review and order-to-delivery coordination.
* Working knowledge of SAP, Microsoft Excel and document control.
* Awareness of quality documentation, material traceability, delivery terms and workshop HSEQ requirements.

**Certifications (preferred But Not Mandatory)**

* Training in supply chain, customer service, technical sales or production coordination.
* Relevant ERP, Excel or quality-management training.

**Special Requirements**

* Willingness and ability to travel frequently across the GCC for site inspections, customer meetings and technical/commercial discussions.
* Flexibility to work in industrial environments while adhering to HSEQ standards.
* Strong customer orientation with the ability to build trust and credibility in a multicultural environment.
* Capacity to work under pressure with tight deadlines for proposals, negotiations and project support.
* High level of technical writing and presentation skills to communicate complex services solutions to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
* Commitment to maintaining confidentiality of customer data and complying with company ethics and policies.

To lead and oversee all ground improvement engineering activities on behalf of the Project Management Consultancy (PMC), ensuring that ground treatment designs, methodologies, and construction works are executed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with project specifications, international standards, and client requirements.   + Vibro Compaction
  + Vibro Replacement (Stone Columns)
  + Dynamic Compaction
  + Rapid Impact Compaction
  + Deep Soil Mixing
  + Jet Grouting
  + Prefabricated Vertical Drains (PVD)
  + Vacuum Consolidation
  + Compaction Grouting
  + Controlled Modulus Columns (CMC)
  + Rigid Inclusions
  + Soil Stabilization using Cement/Lime

* Monitor contractor performance during execution of ground improvement works.
* Verify that approved construction methodologies are followed.
* Review daily, weekly, and monthly progress reports.
* Witness field trials, production works, load tests, and acceptance testing.
* Ensure proper implementation of quality control procedures.
* Review and approve inspection and test plans (ITPs), method statements, and work procedures.

* Review laboratory and field testing results.
* Verify compliance with acceptance criteria.
* Ensure calibration and certification of testing equipment.
* Review as-built documentation and completion reports.

* Monitor project schedule and identify risks affecting ground improvement activities.

* Participate in progress meetings with contractors and stakeholders.
* Review contractor claims related to ground improvement works.

* Ensure all ground improvement activities comply with project HSE requirements.
* Participate in safety audits and site inspections.
* Promote safe execution practices for specialized geotechnical works.

**Documentation & Reporting**

* Prepare technical reports and engineering assessments.
* Review contractor submissions and RFIs.

**Position Overview**

we are committed to building a sustainable and locally rooted food ecosystem. The Marketing Manager will lead the planning, development, and execution of the company’s overall marketing strategy, covering brand development, product marketing, digital marketing, events, campaigns, community engagement, partnerships, and customer experience.

The ideal candidate should have a strong understanding of food, organic and healthy lifestyle products, wellness trends, retail/F&B marketing, events, and community engagement, combined with strong strategic, creative, and analytical capabilities.

The Marketing Manager will ensure that all marketing activities are aligned with the company’s brand identity and business objectives while supporting revenue growth, customer acquisition, engagement, and retention.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Marketing Strategy & Planning**

* Develop and execute the annual marketing strategy aligned with the company’s vision and business growth objectives.
* Work with the Brand Director/Management on brand positioning, target audiences, and competitive differentiation.
* Develop annual and monthly marketing calendars.
* Establish measurable KPIs for brand awareness, customer engagement, lead generation, footfall, sales, and revenue growth.
* Monitor food, health, wellness, retail, and consumer trends and translate insights into marketing initiatives.
* Conduct competitor and market analysis.

**2. Marketing Campaigns & Budget Management**

* Plan and execute integrated marketing campaigns across digital, social media, events, retail, and other channels.
* Prepare and manage the annual marketing budget.
* Monitor campaign expenditure and ensure activities remain within approved budgets.
* Evaluate campaign performance, ROI, customer acquisition, engagement, and sales impact.
* Coordinate promotional calendars with Operations, Finance, Procurement, and other relevant departments.

**3. Brand Management**

* Maintain consistent company brand identity across all customer touchpoints.
* Ensure correct use of logos, brand guidelines, messaging, visual identity, packaging, signage, menus, and promotional materials.
* Review and approve marketing content before publication.
* Support the development and positioning of the company Market, Kitchen, Café, Vitamin Bar, Bakery, events, and other business concepts.
* Protect and strengthen the company’s brand reputation.

**4. Product Marketing**

* Develop marketing plans for new and existing food, beverage, wellness, and retail products.
* Coordinate new product launches with Product, Kitchen, Operations, Procurement, and Sales teams.
* Develop product positioning, customer messaging, promotional strategies, and launch campaigns.
* Monitor product performance and customer response.
* Support seasonal products, promotions, bundles, and limited time offers.
* Coordinate product photography, menu presentation, packaging, and promotional content.

**5. Digital Marketing & Social Media**

* Manage the company’s digital marketing strategy across relevant online channels.
* Oversee social media content calendars and campaign execution.
* Manage paid digital campaigns and monitor advertising performance.
* Oversee SEO, website content, email marketing, and digital customer engagement.
* Coordinate photography, videography, reels, and other creative content.
* Monitor digital analytics and prepare performance reports.
* Ensure third-party platforms maintain accurate brand, product, menu, pricing, and promotional information.

**6. Events & Market**

* Develop marketing plans for the company Market seasons, events, activations, workshops, and community programs.
* Coordinate pre-event, live-event, and post-event marketing activities.
* Promote vendor participation, customer attendance, workshops, food experiences, gardening activities, and family/community programs.
* Coordinate signage, event branding, promotional materials, digital promotion, and customer communication.
* Work closely with Operations and Events teams to improve visitor experience and market visibility.

**7. Community Engagement & Partnerships**

* Build relationships with local communities, schools, organizations, wellness partners, suppliers, and other stakeholders.
* Identify suitable strategic partnerships and collaboration opportunities.
* Develop community engagement campaigns aligned with the company’s sustainability and healthy-lifestyle positioning.
* Coordinate influencer, media, PR, and partnership activities.
* Support corporate and institutional collaborations.

**8. Customer Experience & Market Research**

* Monitor customer feedback, reviews, surveys, and engagement.
* Identify opportunities to improve the overall customer journey and experience.
* Analyse customer behaviour, preferences, purchasing patterns, and market trends.
* Work with Operations and Product teams to implement customer-focused improvements.
* Develop customer retention and loyalty initiatives.

**9. Content & Creative Management**

* Lead the development of marketing content, campaign concepts, advertisements, menus, brochures, posters, signage, digital assets, and presentations.
* Prepare clear creative briefs for designers, photographers, and agencies.
* Maintain a structured library of approved marketing assets.
* Ensure content quality, accuracy, consistency, and timely delivery.

**10. Sales & Revenue Support**

* Develop marketing initiatives that support sales and revenue objectives.
* Analyze sales performance before, during, and after marketing campaigns.
* Coordinate promotional offers with Finance and Operations to ensure commercial viability.
* Support online delivery and third-party platform promotions.
* Identify opportunities to increase customer traffic, average transaction value, repeat purchases, and product awareness.

**11. Team Management**

* Lead and supervise the Marketing Team.
* Set individual objectives, KPIs, priorities, and deadlines.
* Conduct regular team meetings and performance follow-ups.
* Ensure effective allocation of campaigns and marketing projects.
* Coach and develop team members while maintaining accountability for deliverables.

**12. Reporting & Performance Analysis**

* Prepare weekly and monthly marketing reports for Management.
* Track campaign performance against established KPIs.
* Report on social media performance, customer engagement, website traffic, event performance, marketing expenditure, and campaign ROI.
* Present recommendations based on data and customer insights.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Business Administration, Communications, Digital Marketing, or a related field.
* Minimum 5–7 years of marketing experience, preferably within Food & Beverage, FMCG, hospitality, retail, organic/healthy food, wellness, or lifestyle brands.
* Minimum 2–3 years of experience managing a marketing team or function preferred.
* Strong experience in digital marketing, social media, events, content, and campaign management.
* Experience in product marketing and new product launches.
* Experience managing marketing budgets and external agencies.
* Strong written and verbal English communication skills; Arabic would be an advantage.

**HVAC Systems and Maintenance**

Build a significant business. Transform workforce operations at scale.

IRx and Australia's Ashley Technology Pty Ltd (part of Ashley Services Group) are seeking a Chief Executive Officer to lead IRx Workforce Operations, their joint venture bringing proven workforce management technology (ATHEXIS) to Qatar, with GCC expansionto follow.

We want a leader who understands workforce-intensive businesses, has the trust of owners and executives, and can turn relationships into commercial growth.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The business is built on ATHEXIS, Ashley Technology’s  cloud workforce and operations platform. It was developed from 12 years of operational use and is live with 90+ clients across logistics, retail, mining, construction, rail and defence. Organisations that have implemented ATHEXIS report a 33% cut in time-and-attendance admin and 42,890 overtime hours saved across its client base.

ATHEXIS covers four areas:

* **People:**
   capacity planning, rostering with anti-double-allocation rules, mobile timesheets, and recruitment with AI candidate filtering.
* **Assets and tasks:**
   allocation of assets and tasks alongside people, with actual vs planned hours.
* **Contracts:**
   real-time costing and reporting across sites, employment agreements and jurisdictions.
* **Compliance:**
   qualifications, clearances, right to work and safety workflows. Workers with expired credentials are blocked from being rostered.

Qatar is a strong fit. It has a large, mobile workforce, heavy compliance obligations (visas, labour regulation, accommodation, transport, supply-chain assurance), and an energy expansion that will drive major turnarounds. Much of this is still managed on spreadsheets.

The JV will go to market as a Qatar company on proven international technology, tailored for Qatari operations, starting with oil and gas. It combines IRx's relationships and industrial ecosystem with Ashley Technology’s operating experience and platform.

**YOUR MANDATE**

You report to the JV Board. You are accountable for strategy, commercial results, delivery, organisation, P&L and cash.

* Build a focused pipeline of 10–15 priority accounts, aiming for five or six real prospects in play at any time. Sales cycles in Qatar are long, so no single deal can carry the plan.
* Engage owners, CEOs and operational leaders, and lead major pursuits through to negotiation, contract signature and collection.
* Work with IRx's senior executives, who open doors at CEO and C-suite level. You own the relationship day to day and drive it to close. Work with Ashley Technology on technical aspects of the product and its delivery and with IRx for business operations.
* Lead with the customer's problem, not the product. Build business cases on cost visibility, compliance risk, productivity and capacity planning.

**> Build Commercial Scale**

* Run proof-of-concept and pilot programmes, typically 12 weeks on the customer's own historical data. Qualify prospects hard so pilots convert to paid contracts.
* Shape pricing to each customer: subscription plus per-person or transactional fees, with consumption-based entry offers in year one. Price on value delivered, not cost to serve.
* Expand deployments across customer sites, contracts and business units. Cross-sell the wider IRx offering with the Board's agreement.

**> Lead Workforce Transformation**

* Help customers improve deployment, utilisation, productivity, cost visibility and compliance through better workflows and realdigital adoption.
* Use benchmarking, such as cost per transaction or cost per unit of work, to show customers where the value is.

**> Deliver & Retain**

* Build in-country first-line support and an implementation capability. Use delivery partners (typically international Systems Integrators with whom IRx have a partnership) where it makes sense, project by project.
* Work with Ashley Technology technical team on second and third-line support, on the roadmap and on Qatar-specific configuration. There is one global product, with no forks.
* Meet Qatar data-residency and security requirements, with in-country hosting and a credible path through Microsoft's ecosystem.
* Own deployment success, measured value, renewals and expansion.

**> Lead The JV**

* Recruit and develop the team and manage budgets and margins. Year one aims to be cost-neutral, with Ashley Technology and IRx co-funding the early stage until revenue carries the business.
* Report clearly to the Board and bring recommendations, not just updates.
* Work within the Board's governance: reserved matters, dual signatories and delegated authority limits. Manage the Qatar tender mechanics, including bid and performance bonds, parent guarantees and JV capitalisation.

**> Win In The Qatar Market**

* Engage the national ecosystem, including Tawteen, QDB, QRDI and innovation funding.
* Build the JV's local identity and brand with IRx and Ashley Technology.

**> Develop The Next Phase**

* Inventory Control & Planning:
* Partner with Spare Part department to maintain safety stock levels while mitigating slow moving and obsolete inventory.

* Utilize SAP ERP (MM/SD/WM), WMS/TMS platforms, and Power BI dashboards to track delivery milestones, inventory aging, and logistics performance.

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, International Business, or a related field.
* Experience:
* Minimum 5–7 years of logistics and supply chain experience, with at least 3 years in a management/lead role within the Automotive Industry in Canada.
* Hands-on experience managing both Finished Vehicles (VDC/Car Haulers) and Spare Parts Warehousing (PDC).

2. Technical & Core Competencies
  

* Customs & Compliance: In-depth knowledge of Canadian customs processes, CBSA regulations, CARM portal, eManifest, Incoterms (FOB, CIF, EXW), and GST/HST tax rules.

**The Role:**

As a member of our Real Estate & Facilities Management team within Corporate Operations at IGM, you will be joining a highly collaborative group focused on keeping our workplaces safe, compliant and well managed for employees, advisors, clients, contractors and visitors.

As Manager, Workplace Health and Safety, you will lead, maintain and continuously improve IGM’s Workplace Health and Safety program across our Winnipeg, Toronto and Montréal corporate campuses and supported IG Wealth Management and Mackenzie distribution locations across Canada.

You will work across a matrixed environment with Facility Management, HR, Legal, Risk, Compliance, Security, Business Continuity, landlords, vendors and third-party consultants. The work spans program governance, legislative compliance, health and safety committee support, hazard and incident management, workplace inspections, training, emergency preparedness, corrective action tracking and reporting.

This is a role for someone who enjoys independent judgement, building trusted relationships, and turning data and lessons learned into practical improvements.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**WPHS Program Governance, Standards & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead IGM’s Workplace Health and Safety program for corporate campuses and supported IGWM and Mackenzie distribution locations across Canada, applying advanced knowledge of workplace health and safety, legislative requirements and market practices.
* Establish, maintain and improve policies, procedures, standards, tools, templates and governance routines to support consistent execution across jurisdictions.
* Manage third-party consultant support, including scope, cadence, deliverables, findings, benchmarking, recommendations and implementation follow-up.
* Use incident trends, inspection results, committee feedback, audit outcomes and industry practices to strengthen program maturity, controls and reporting.

**Legislative Compliance, By-Laws & Risk Management**

* Monitor applicable Canadian workplace health and safety requirements, including provincial legislation and relevant municipal by-laws, and translate obligations into practical operating standards.
* Identify workplace hazards, compliance gaps and emerging risks; support risk assessments; recommend corrective actions; and track remediation to completion.
* Collaborate with HR, Legal, Risk, Compliance, Facility Management, Security, Business Continuity, landlords, vendors and consultants to support regulatory readiness.
* Escalate sensitive, urgent or higher-risk matters with clear facts, options, recommendations and business impacts.

**Committees, Representatives & Internal Responsibility System**

* Support Joint Health and Safety Committees, health and safety representatives, fire wardens, first aiders and people leaders with guidance, templates, agenda support, issue tracking and escalation pathways.
* Reinforce shared accountability for safe work practices and the effective operation of the internal responsibility system across IGM’s portfolio.
* Clarify roles, responsibilities, expectations and decision paths to improve consistency and follow-through across sites.

**Incident, Hazard & Inspection Management**

* Oversee processes for reporting, documenting, investigating and following up on workplace incidents, hazards, inspections, employee concerns and corrective actions.
* Work closely with local leaders, Facility Management, HR, Legal, Risk, Security, Business Continuity, landlords, vendors and consultants to ensure timely response and practical resolution.
* Resolve difficult and sometimes complex matters by identifying root issues, evaluating alternatives and recommending new approaches where established processes do not fully address the issue.
* Track incidents, hazards, inspections and corrective actions through completion, identifying trends and recurring issues that require additional controls, communication, training or escalation.

**Training, Awareness & Communications**

* Coordinate mandatory workplace safety training, committee education, leader awareness, employee communications, emergency procedure awareness and targeted safety campaigns.
* Ensure materials are current, practical, accessible and aligned to workplace risks, legislative requirements, IGM values and business needs.
* Communicate clear guidance on policies, procedures and practices to employees, leaders, committees, consultants, vendors and senior stakeholders, particularly during sensitive or urgent matters.

**Reporting, Metrics & Performance Discipline**

* Develop and maintain reporting on incidents, hazards, inspections, training completion, committee effectiveness, corrective action status, emerging risks, consultant findings and program maturity.
* Use data, consultant recommendations, audit outcomes and lessons learned to improve controls, service standards and documentation.
* Apply sound judgment by prioritizing work, managing issue closure and recommending practical improvements that balance stakeholder experience, cost, risk, compliance and operational continuity.

**Vendor, Landlord & Cross-Functional Coordination**

* Coordinate with landlords, property managers, vendors, consultants and internal partners to support safe workplace operations, regulatory response, emergency preparedness and issue resolution.
* Manage scope, deliverables, cadence and performance of third-party workplace health and safety consultant services.
* Lead through influence by building productive relationships, clarifying accountabilities and maintaining timely, professional communication across matrixed teams and external partners.

**Additional Requirements**

* This role requires 3-5 days a week on site to support campus operations, committee activities, inspections, training, incident response, and stakeholder engagement.
* Occasional travel between Winnipeg, Toronto, Montréal, and selected IGWM distribution locations across Canada may be required.
* Ability to respond to urgent workplace health and safety incidents, regulatory matters, emergency response activities, or business continuity events outside regular business hours as required.
* Ability to handle confidential, sensitive, or urgent workplace matters with discretion, sound judgement, and professionalism.
* Ability to operate in a regulated financial services environment where documentation, risk awareness, timely escalation, stakeholder experience, and disciplined follow-through are important to maintaining trust and operational readiness.

**Overview**
Tonal Care runs seven days a week across an in-house Toronto team and an outsourced partner operation. The Manager, Care Operations owns how that operation performs day to day.
  
  
You will own daily delivery across all tiers, the operational relationship with our outsourced partner, and the staffing and capacity plans that keep service levels intact. You will lead a Team Lead and a team of Customer Experience Specialists, each of whom owns one or two lines of business, and you will work the queue yourself when coverage requires it.
  
  
This is a hands-on, player/coach, operating role. You set the standard, work within it, and hold the operation to it.
  
  
What You Will Do
  
  
Daily Delivery
  
  

* Act as a player-coach during the initial phase, spending dedicated time working directly in the queue alongside specialists to model best practices, coach in real time, and establish baseline workflows
* Own daily delivery across all tiers, setting service levels, coverage models, and workflow standards that hold consistent delivery across phone, email, chat, and video.
* Own the daily, weekly, and monthly plans for SLA, CSAT, Average Handle Time, and First Contact Resolution, and be accountable for hitting them.
* Identify performance trends, operational risks, and root causes, and build the action plans that close the gap.
* Lead regular performance reviews and operational business reviews with internal stakeholders and partner leadership.
* Support incident and volume management during elevated contact periods, product issues, launches, and other business disruptions.
* Work the queue yourself when coverage requires it — absences, PTO, peak volume, or an uncovered line of business. You are the final backstop on coverage.
* Translate operational data into clear insights and recommendations for Care leadership.

Outsourced Partner Performance
  
  

* Serve as the day-to-day operational point of contact for Tonal’s outsourced partner, managing performance through their team leads and supervisors.
* Hold partner leadership accountable to agreed KPIs, SLAs, quality standards, staffing commitments, and Tonal’s brand voice.
* Run weekly performance reviews with partner teams.
* Report weekly to our Logistics, Field Operations, and Care Leadership team across all Care Operations metrics.
* Partner with their leadership on performance improvement plans, staffing strategies, coaching opportunities, and operational readiness.
* Monitor partner staffing, attrition, attendance, and utilization to catch capacity risk before it reaches Members.
* Make sure partner teams are aligned to Tonal policies, workflows, and operating standards, and are prepared for new programs, product changes, and launches.
* Escalate to the Senior Manager, Care Operations when partner performance issues cannot be resolved at the working level. Contract terms, rates, and renewals sit with the Director of Care Operations.

Staffing and Capacity
  
  

* Own workforce planning with partner Workforce Management and Tonal analytics, setting capacity and staffing models against forecast demand and adjusting intraday to protect service levels.
* Plan coverage across the full seven-day operating window, including weekends, holidays, and peak periods.
* Own the volume, staffing, and partner utilization assumptions that feed Care’s operating budget.
* Monitor forecast accuracy and adjust staffing assumptions based on actual contact volume, productivity, shrinkage, and service-level performance.
* Ensure schedules keep the teams at a sustainable working load rather than at full utilization, so there is room to absorb spikes and absences.

Team Leadership
  
  

* Lead and develop the team through the Team Lead and senior specialists, owning performance calibration, coaching, career development, and coverage planning.
* Make sure every line of business has a named owner, that the assignment is understood, and that owners are held to how their domain performs.
* Be accountable for the escalations programme. Specialists and the Team Lead resolve individual escalations; you own how the programme performs and where it needs to change.
* Sit in the health, safety, and legal escalation chain: Specialist → Team Lead → Manager, Care Operations → Senior Manager, Care Operations → Director, Care Operations.
* Ensure clear ownership and communication on sensitive, complex, or high-risk Member situations.
* Monitor escalation trends to surface recurring Member pain points, and work with the frontline to reduce avoidable escalations and lift first contact resolution.

Process and Partnership
  
  

* Translate the operating plan set with the Senior Manager, Care Operations into daily execution, and own that execution.
* Work with the Care Enablement team to identify knowledge gaps and roll out new troubleshooting SOPs, training, and tool updates to the front line.
* Coordinate with Logistics and Field Operations to deliver a seamless end-to-end experience for both specialists and Members.
* Simplify workflows to reduce Member effort, improve specialist efficiency, and remove unnecessary operational friction.
* Represent Care Operations in cross-functional initiatives and launches, and support the rollout and adoption of new tools, processes, and support programs.

Coverage and Schedule
  
  
Tonal Care operates seven days a week, 9:00 AM to 10:00 PM EST. This is a hands-on leadership role and the coverage expectations come with it:
  
  

* You and your team may be required to work weekends, holidays, and after hours as coverage requires. You and your team’s schedule will shift with the needs of the operation.
* Your team will carry on-call responsibility for incidents, outages, product issues, and elevated volume periods.
* Priorities change during the day. Peak season, launches, and product escalations will change what a day looks like.

Who You Are
  
  

* You have 5+ years of experience in Customer Care, Customer Support, or Contact Center Operations, including 2+ years leading teams, vendors, or outsourced operations.
* You are operationally minded and move comfortably between the operating plan and the queue. You set the standard, then hold the operation to it.
* You have managed operational KPIs and used data to find and fix performance problems. You don’t just report numbers — you understand the why behind them and change process, staffing, or enablement to move the trend.
* You are an empathetic coach who knows how to motivate a team and can turn complex data into feedback a specialist can act on.
